s: sprout (outgrowth on a seed or fruit); for a shoot of an actual growing plant, the doublet Spross m is more usual

Sprosse.et: From Middle High German sprozze m, from Old High German sprozzo (“rung”), from Proto-Germanic *sprutô, from the root of *spreutaną, whence sprießen. Cognate with Dutch sport (“rung”), Middle Low German sprōte (“rung, sprout”), Old English sprot(a) (“sprout”). …

spröde.et: Uncertain. Possibly connected with West Flemish sprooi and Middle English sprēth, sprēþe (“spiritually weak, inadequate”).
